problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be bases of ${R}^{2}.$ If ${b}_{1}=5{c}_{2}-3{c}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}=2{c}_{1}-4{c}_{2},$ find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ from $B$ to $C.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Change-of-Coordinates Matrix Given a Linear Connection Between Two Bases
examples.problem: Let $\mathcal{B}=\{\mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2\}$ and $\mathcal{C}=\{\mathbf{c}_1,\mathbf{c}_2\}$ be bases of $\mathbb{R}^2.$ If $\mathbf{c}_1=\mathbf{b}_2-4\mathbf{b}_1$ and $\mathbf{c}_2=5\mathbf{b}_1+7\mathbf{b}_2,$ find the change-of-coordinates matrix $P_{\small\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{B}}$ from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the vectors in $\mathcal{C}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}$ are

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}$ is a matrix whose respective columns are the coordinates of the vectors of $\mathcal{C}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}.$
